findings.text: the dry-run preview calls _measurement_flag_refusal without the node's role, so a preview of a --role review dispatch of a declared-done section is refused with exit 2 while the launch at reckon/crew/dispatching/preparation.py:725 passes role=str(node.role) and accepts it; the role carve-out at preparation.py:307 is reached by no test in either direction, and the preview contradicts the dispatch it previews in the opposite direction to the mismatch the comment above the call says it exists to prevent.

the reflex case asserts a substring of the refusal prose ("measurement" in report["reason"]) rather than the structural flag the refusal sets at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3375 (report["measure_only"] is True), so any other refusal path whose wording carries the word satisfies it; the recorded negative control reddens it only because the fallback reason is the run's liveness, and a rewording of the measurement refusal without the word would redden the case against correct code.

the measure_only marker is read by three independently written definitions with three tolerances - _measurement_reason here, _measurement_run_skip at reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:1928 and _is_measurement_run at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3341 - where reckon/run_record.py already owns run-record field accessors of this shape (measurement_exclusion_reason at reckon/run_record.py:673) and is the natural single owner; the three copies can drift on a malformed marker while the reflex, the lander and the promotion disagree about whether one run is a measurement.

an unreadable plan answers "" and the assignment guard is skipped rather than raised, so the one case in which the section's declaration cannot be established is the case in which a declared-done section stays dispatchable without the flag; the docstring's defence is a claim about a validation that runs later in dispatch, and no test drives the unreadable-plan path to show which refusal a caller actually sees.
